result.document_summary: New Jersey P.L. 2025, c.405, an enacted statute capping residential rental application fees at $50 (CPI-adjusted annually), with penalties and exemptions for one- and two-family dwellings and licensed real estate agents.
result.notes: Approved January 20, 2026; takes effect on the first day of the fourth month next following enactment, i.e., 2026-05-01 (computed from the document's formula). The $50 cap is adjusted annually for CPI beginning January 1 of the year next following enactment (2027), only if CPI change is greater than zero. Not extracted: penalty and rulemaking provisions are part of the same rule.

rules.title: Residential rental application fee capped at $50
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not require an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property that exceeds $50. The cap is adjusted annually for CPI, and violators face civil penalties of $500 to $1,000 with the wrongfully charged amount refunded to the applicant.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord, or agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to residential rental properties in New Jersey, except dwelling units in one-family or two-family dwellings and Real Estate Commission licensees who are not the landlord.

all_of.text: a dwelling unit located in a one-family or two-family dwelling that is offered for rent

all_of.value: licensee of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission who is not the landlord

rules.exemptions_text: Exempts dwelling units in one-family or two-family dwellings, and licensees of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission unless the licensee is the landlord.
